title: BT CEO eyes deeper job cuts as AI becomes more powerful, FT reports
description: BT CEO Allison Kirkby plans to increase job cuts beyond the initial 40,000 as advances in AI technologies enable further operational efficiency and cost reductions, aiming to strip out 3 billion pounds by 2030.
content_summary: BT Group CEO Allison Kirkby announced plans for deeper job cuts at BT due to advances in artificial intelligence. Initially, BT aimed to cut over 40,000 jobs and save 3 billion pounds by 2030. Kirkby now foresees AI enabling further automation and workforce reductions. This reflects BT's strategy to modernize operations and improve financial health amid technological changes. The move aligns with a broader industry trend of AI-driven automation to optimize costs and resources.

title: The Boys Star Erin Moriarty Shares Graves' Disease Diagnosis
description: Erin Moriarty from 'The Boys' revealed her Graves' disease diagnosis, discussing symptoms, treatment progress, and urging fans to get checked.
content_summary: Erin Moriarty, who plays Starlight in 'The Boys,' announced her diagnosis with Graves' disease, an autoimmune thyroid condition. Initially mistaking symptoms for stress, she began treatment and felt better within 24 hours. Moriarty emphasizes the varied nature of autoimmune diseases and encourages others experiencing symptoms to seek medical attention. Her openness has helped raise awareness about Graves' disease and the importance of early detection and treatment.

title: Pacers assist business that was victimized by NBA Finals scam
description: No widely reported cases of Indiana Pacers assisting a business victimized by NBA Finals scam as of June 2025; scams often involve fake tickets or merchandise.
content_summary: As of June 2025, there is no public record of the Indiana Pacers assisting a small business victimized by an NBA Finals scam. While scams are common during major sports events, no specific incident involving the Pacers has been reported this year. The Pacers are active in community support, but no related assistance has been documented. Consumers should remain cautious against scams at large sporting events.
